topic: Dot Products and the Concept of Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite: Projective Intuition
lecture_lines: Vector A casts a shadow on vector B.
This shadow length signifies the projection.
animations: Draw vector A (#FF0000) and vector B (#0000FF).
Create a perpendicular line from the tip of A onto B (#FFFFFF).
Draw a segment representing the projection of A onto B (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Defining the Dot Product as a Linear Map
lecture_lines: Dot product is a linear map.
It returns a scalar from two vectors.
A fixed vector w defines this function.
animations: Represent the dot product as a linear function f(v) = w · v (#FFFFFF).
Show v moving along the input domain mapping to scalar outputs (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Core Concept: Duality
lecture_lines: Duality connects vectors to linear functionals.
The dot product acts as a bridge.
Every functional corresponds to a vector.
animations: Visualize vector v as an arrow (#FF0000).
Visualize the linear functional as a coordinate line (#00FF00).
Show the dot product as the interaction between v and the functional (#FFFFFF).
Display the duality transform mapping vector to functional (#FFFF00).
Show the final merger of the vector and operation (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Visualizing Duality via Level Sets
lecture_lines: Dot product defines perpendicular level sets.
Level sets map the dual space.
animations: Draw a set of parallel lines representing a constant dot product (#FFFFFF).
Place vector w perpendicular to these level sets (#FF0000).
Animate a scalar constant c increasing to move the level sets (#00FF00).

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Vectors are points, duals are tools.
Dot product bridges geometry and functions.
animations: Display a vector space and its dual side by side (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the dot product connecting these two worlds (#FF0000).
Show the unification of static vectors and operational functions (#FFFF00).
